sections.h2: Which Warren offices set and collect your property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessing Department prepares the roll and tracks 59,077 parcels, roughly 54,620 real and 4,457 personal. The Treasurer's Office mails the bills and acts as collection agent for every unit levying inside the city: Warren itself, the county and the millages of six school districts.

Macomb County sits above both. Once the city's collection window shuts, the Macomb County Treasurer inherits whatever is unpaid. For a look at one house, the Assessing Department runs a free BS&A lookup by owner name, address or parcel number, showing values and tax history for current and recent years.

Two mailings go out annually, in the first week of July and again in the first week of December. A missing bill does not cancel the obligation, according to the city. Ask the Treasurer's Office, 586-574-4542, for a copy.

sections.h2: When are Warren property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Summer bills combine the city and school levies; winter bills carry the county's. The city offers an uncommon two-part summer option, and the first part is about 62 percent of the summer total.

Warren Treasurer's calendar of payment windows and late charges
BillWindowConsequence of missing it
Summer, full or first partJuly 1 through August 31Beginning September 1 the full summer balance is required, with a 1% charge in September and half a percent per month after that
Summer, second partBilled December 1; pay by January 31A 3.5% charge starts February 1 on unpaid summer tax
Winter (county levies)December 1 through February 28Delinquent balances move to the Macomb County Treasurer along with the city's fees

A check is conditional until it clears the bank, and a postmark dated no later than the due date avoids late penalties. The levies also run on different fiscal years: July 1 to June 30 for the city and schools, calendar year for the county and October to September for the state education tax.

sections.h2: What happens to Warren taxes that are still unpaid in March?
sections.html:
They are delinquent and must be paid to the Macomb County Treasurer. Warren's payment page says the county tacks on the city's collection fees, an additional 4 percent fee, and 1 percent interest for every month the balance stays open.

At its public tax presentation the city explained that its Treasurer has no legal power to collect past that point. It also noted that county staff offer payment plans and other assistance to residents trying to keep their homes, and urged people to call quickly instead of letting foreclosure steps begin.

A seller should expect any open county balance to be cleared at closing. Pull the parcel's BS&A record a few weeks ahead of signing a purchase agreement so the number holds no surprises.

sections.h2: Is there a way to defer Warren summer taxes?
sections.html:
Qualifying owners can push the summer due date back to February 14. Every item here must apply:

  • Household income of $40,000 a year or less.
  • The home is the owner's primary residence.
  • The owner is 62 or older, or an eligible serviceperson, veteran, widow or widower, a blind person, or someone totally and permanently disabled, paraplegic, hemiplegic or quadriplegic.

The city mails forms each July to people who filed the year before, and first-time applicants phone 586-574-4554 from July onward. Return the form by September 15.

Other relief runs through the Assessing Department. A poverty exemption on a principal residence is decided by the Board of Review at its March, July or December meeting and covers one year only. A disabled veteran's homestead exemption under MCL 211.7b needs an affidavit and Veterans Affairs documents filed by December 30.

sections.h2: How do you contest a Warren assessment?
sections.html:
Only the March Board of Review can change an opinion of value on a house. A residential owner must protest there before moving on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Five residents appointed by the mayor and confirmed by City Council sit on the board, which hears complaints and can adjust individual assessments.

The 2026 sessions were held March 11, 16 and 17 at City Hall, 1 City Square, Suite 310. Appointments were booked at 586-574-4532, and mailed or delivered letters had to arrive by 5:00 p.m. on March 17. Email and online filings are not accepted. The Assessing Department sends an assessment change notice each February, and the city publishes the March schedule at least a week ahead.

  • A written appeal needs your name, address, phone, parcel number, reasons and signature.
  • Supply sales data or an appraisal, since the petitioner must prove true cash value.
  • A representative needs a signed letter from you.
  • The decision arrives by mail, not at the hearing.

Meetings in July and December handle poverty exemptions and qualified errors only. Commercial and industrial real property can skip ahead to the Tax Tribunal by May 31.

sections.h2: How does a Warren sale change the buyer's taxable value?
sections.html:
The cap falls away. Assessed value is half of estimated market value, and taxable value usually climbs each year by the smaller of 5 percent or the inflation multiplier. In the year after a house changes hands, taxable value is raised to match assessed value, a step the city calls uncapping.

The Assessing Department's overview works through examples, and in one of them taxable value jumps 57.89 percent after a sale. Which of Warren's six school districts serves the address affects the millage, so run the state's property tax estimator before you set an asking price. A principal residence exemption lowers the school operating levy for an owner who lives in the home, and a buyer who plans to move in should ask the Assessing Department how to file.

sections.h2: What do closing agents need from a Warren seller?
sections.html:
Start with MCL 211.135. A warranty deed travels with a county treasurer's certificate that five prior years of tax are paid, while a quitclaim without warranty covenants avoids that requirement.

Next, the city's note to mortgage and title firms: send the bill with its scannable barcode. If no bill comes with the check, a $2.00 duplicate bill fee applies, and it becomes $5.00 per parcel when the city has to go and collect the missing paperwork.

Then, the payment channels. The online portal charges nothing for bank account payments and 2.8 percent, minimum $1.50, for cards. You can also pay at 1-844-435-3977, by post, at City Hall, in a Van Dyke bank branch, or in drop boxes behind the Civic Center Library and the Maybelle Burnette Library.

sections.h2: What is Warren like for a seller?
sections.html:
Warren is a 34-square-mile grid between 8 Mile and 14 Mile roads, bordering Detroit on its south side, with Center Line entirely enclosed inside it. Beebe's Corners, a carriage stop at Mound and Chicago roads, started in 1830, and the city incorporated on January 1, 1957 after the Chrysler truck plant, the Detroit Arsenal tank plant and the General Motors Technical Center drew families. I-696, M-53 (Van Dyke), M-97 and Mound Road carry most traffic.

Southeast Warren, including Warrendale, Berkshire Manor and Belangers Garden, has many bungalows from just after World War II, with brick ranches north of Stephens Road built after 1960. Red Run and Bear Creek now work as an open storm drain toward the Clinton River and Lake St. Clair.

The Census Bureau estimates 137,138 residents in 2025 among 54,744 households. Homes are 71.1 percent owner-occupied with a median value of $193,400, median income is $64,016 and median rent is $1,225. A given parcel's own assessment and millage set its bill, not these averages.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for the first Warren summer installment?
faqs.a: August 31. The summer bill may be paid whole or in two parts, with part two billed December 1 and due January 31. After August 31 the entire summer balance is required.

faqs.q: Where does a Warren winter tax payment go after February 28?
faqs.a: To the Macomb County Treasurer. The city stops accepting it after the last day of February, and the county adds the city's fees, a 4 percent fee and 1 percent monthly interest.

faqs.q: Is online filing allowed for a Warren assessment appeal?
faqs.a: No. Appeals are accepted in person by appointment or by letter received before the deadline. Residential owners must go through the March Board of Review before the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

faqs.q: Will a Warren tax bill change after the house sells?
faqs.a: Yes. The next year the buyer's taxable value is set equal to the assessed value, which is half of market value. That can sit far above the capped figure the seller paid.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for a Warren summer tax deferment?
faqs.a: Primary-residence owners earning $40,000 or less who are 62 or older or fall into a listed veteran, widow, blind or disabled group. The form is due September 15 and moves the due date to February 14.
